This figure beats the <cite id="1">peer program ratio median of 89.5%</cite> [1]. Operational resilience is backed by <cite id="1">12.2 months of working capital reserves</cite>, ensuring financial continuity for faculty and students [1]. rich_narrative.summary: Nur Islamic School of Louisville offers full-time educational programming for youth ranging from early childhood through high school [3]. In FY2024, the institution generated <cite id="2">$2,894,945 in total revenue</cite>, up from <cite id="2">$2,796,768 in FY2023</cite>, reflecting steady institutional growth [2]. The school provides a holistic environment that blends academic subjects with Quranic and Arabic studies, supported by strong academic distinctions such as earning <cite id="3">AP School Honor Roll Platinum Level recognition</cite> [3]. Operational spending is directed entirely toward educational initiatives, reporting a <cite id="2">100.0% program expense ratio in FY2024 tax filings</cite> [2]. Financial health is further stabilized by holding approximately <cite id="1">12.2 months of working capital</cite> [1]. While the school demonstrates strong financial efficiency and solid educational delivery, its focus on local schooling means its scope is concentrated primarily within the Louisville metropolitan area rather than broader international relief initiatives [2].
